questions.question: When entering a curve, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
Where you can see and be seen best.
In the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can see and be seen best.
questions.explanation: When entering a curve, position your motorcycle to see clearly and be visible to others. On a left curve, ride on the right side of your lane to see oncoming traffic early. On a right curve, ride left of center to see ahead without getting too close to oncoming vehicles.

questions.question: If you are towing a trailer on your motorcycle, how should your following distance change?
questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, increase your following distance. The extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: When you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do not brake and swerve at the same time. Instead, brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake. Doing both together can cause loss of control.

questions.question: When rain starts, what is the safest way to ride?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull over and wait for the rain to stop.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Roads are slippery when rain starts, especially in the center of lanes. Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles. The left tire track is often the best choice.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the road with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind it.
Wait until it starts moving again.
Move to a different lane away from it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from it.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: There is usually an oily strip in the center of a traffic lane. What should motorcyclists do?

options.text: Find the lane with less oil buildup.

questions.explanation: Avoid the oily strip in the center of the lane. Since it is usually only two feet wide, you can often stay to the left or right side of it while still being in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: If a driver makes eye contact with you, what does this mean?

options.text: It does not mean they will yield to you properly.
They will definitely yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will yield to you properly.
questions.explanation: Do not assume eye contact means a driver will properly yield to you. A driver can look directly at you and still not see you or fail to respond correctly.

questions.question: When you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, what is the correct action?

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake.
questions.explanation: Take these actions one at a time, not together. Do not brake while swerving, as this can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in broad daylight. Wear bright colors and reflective materials even during the day to stay visible.

questions.question: Is eye protection required for motorcycle operators?
questions.explanation: Proper eye protection is required for all motorcycle operators.

questions.question: Your motorcycle starts to weave while riding over uneven metal bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear right away.
Ride in a zigzag pattern across the bridge.

questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves on uneven bridge gratings, stay relaxed and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than the weaving.

questions.question: When carrying a load on your motorcycle, how should it be secured?
questions.explanation: Loads should be secured as low as possible. Attaching a load to a sissy bar can raise the motorcycle's center of gravity and affect its balance.

questions.question: You are riding in hot weather and wearing a protective jacket. What should you do?

options.text: Take frequent breaks to cool off.
Remove the jacket to stay cool in the sun.
Keep the jacket on to protect yourself from heat and injury.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the jacket on to protect yourself from heat and injury.
questions.explanation: A good riding jacket protects you in a crash, no matter the weather. Jackets also help prevent dehydration in hot weather. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool.

questions.question: The center of the lane has an oily strip. What is true about this strip?

options.text: It is safe to ride on unless it is raining.
Ride on it only when sharing the lane with another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to ride on unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily center strip usually provides enough grip for safe riding, except when it is raining. The strip is usually less than two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and still stay in the center lane.

questions.question: Your front wheel locks while braking. What should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
Release the front brake right away and use only the rear brake.
Keep the front wheel locked until you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the brake immediately and then reapply it.

questions.question: You reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle. What should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: A vehicle is passing you from behind. Which lane position is safest?
questions.explanation: The center lane position is safest when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding on the far side may prompt the driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance for a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Maintain at least a two-second following distance under normal conditions. When conditions are poor, use a larger following distance.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When riding at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance to prevent collisions. Use the headlights of other vehicles to see ahead. Be ready to change lanes, especially at night.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the right lane ends ahead.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have more time to react to other drivers.
You have limited escape route options.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have limited escape route options.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between vehicles helps you react to other drivers in time and gives you room to maneuver safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. This sign warns you that traffic ahead will be merging.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders be positioned?
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch and help them from behind.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming up ahead.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Get closer to the vehicle in front so you can see farther using its lights.
Keep your normal speed to reduce the chance of being hit from behind.
Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: At night, slow down and keep more distance between you and other vehicles. You cannot see as well at night, so you need extra time and space to react to dangers ahead.
